title: What IF College Assigned Your Crush as YOUR WIFE
description:
Your college just sent you a notification. Assigned spouse: Crush. Relationship: WIFE. 💍

BRO. THAT'S LITERALLY MY CRUSH.

Welcome to the Campus Partner Project, where students are assigned a fake husband or wife for 30 days. You have to share an apartment, manage a budget, complete relationship challenges, and survive weekly compatibility tests.

Starting compatibility: 50%.

One problem: I'm already in love with her. And somehow, between burning breakfast, getting jealous of another guy, and completely misunderstanding her, our compatibility drops to 39%. 💀

Now I have 30 days to figure out whether she actually likes me or if I'm just embarrassing myself.

question for the comments:

Day 30. The college gives you two options: YES or NO. Would you continue dating your assigned partner or walk away?

Subscribe before my compatibility score reaches 0%. My Crush is Watching.

Real fact in this episode: A famous 1950 MIT housing study found that people living closer together were more likely to become friends. Sometimes, simply spending time together can change everything.

title: What If You Could See Everyone for Who They Really Are?
tags: what if you could see everyone for who they really are

description:
What if you woke up and could see who everyone REALLY is, floating above their head? 👀

Your mom: SECRETLY A RETIRED PRO WRESTLER (she opens pickle jars with one finger). Your dad: SECRETLY CRIES AT EVERY DOG MOVIE. Your bus driver: SECRETLY AN OLYMPIC FIGURE SKATER. 🚌⛸️

Then the quiet kid at the back of homeroom whispers "here"... and his label says SECRETLY LEOMAXX. 8 MILLION FOLLOWERS. 🐯

And your crush, Maya? You are not ready for Maya's label. 🥒

Did you know? In 2018, scientists had strangers talk for a few minutes, then asked how much they thought the other person liked them. Most people guessed too low. It's called the "liking gap": people like us more than we think. (Boothby, Cooney, Sandstrom & Clark, Psychological Science, 2018)

title: What If You Went Back in Time Every Time You Died?
tags: what if you went back in time every time you died
what if you went back in time
description:
What if you went back in time every time you died? The first time you die, an asteroid destroys Earth. The next second, you're fourteen years old again, in your childhood bedroom, twenty years before impact. Every death sends you back to the same morning, and you have unlimited chances to save eight billion people.

But every time you restart, the world forgets everything you did: your money, your degrees, your space missions, even the people who loved you. You try science, nuclear warheads, a fortune built on knowing the future, giant engines, a colony on Mars and underground shelters. Each life teaches you something new, and each death costs you the world.

This is a 3D animated what-if story about a time loop, the end of the world and what it really means to save it. Watch to the end, because the asteroid is hiding something, and this is only Part 1.

title: What If YOU Woke Up as a CAT?
tags: what if you were a cat
why do cats always land on their feet
cat falls from building and survives
description:
Theo wakes up on top of the fridge as a black cat with a teal collar. Every "Mom, it's me!" comes out as "meow", his little sister names him Mr. Fluffington, and his best friend's "pss pss pss" drags him across the kitchen against his will. Then the real cat science: the mirror behind a cat's eye that lets it see in a sixth of the light, the righting reflex (and the cat that fell 40 floors into a planter), ears that hear up to 79,000 hertz, and a purr the brain fires about thirty times a second. The catch: no sweet taste, milk is a bad idea, and chocolate's theobromine literally has his name in it. Then a storm knocks out the power, the smoke alarm's battery is dead, and only a cat can see through the smoke.
